topic: Mutual Fund and ETF Fees and Expenses
subtopic: ETF Premiums and Discounts to Net Asset Value
source_evidence: An ETF share is trading at a premium when its market price is higher than the NAV per share. An ETF share is trading at a discount when its market price is lower than the NAV per share.
answer: An ETF can trade at a market price that differs from its net asset value (NAV) per share. If the market price is above NAV, the ETF trades at a premium; if it is below NAV, it trades at a discount. As a result, when you buy ETF shares, you may pay more or less than NAV, and when you sell, you may receive more or less than NAV. A change in the premium or discount can therefore be a potential cost or gain.
